message.content:
Below is a concise list of the **long‑weekend holidays** that Canadians can expect in 2023.  
These are the federal public holidays that either fall on a Friday or Monday (or are observed on a Monday when they fall on a weekend), creating a three‑day weekend.  (If a holiday falls on a Saturday, the following Monday is usually observed, giving a long weekend that includes the Saturday.)

| Long‑Weekend Dates | Holiday (Observed) | Notes |
|--------------------|--------------------|-------|
| **Jan 1 – Jan 2** | New Year’s Day (observed Mon Jan 2) | New Year’s Day falls on Sunday; the holiday is observed on Monday. |
| **Feb 18 – Feb 20** | Family Day (Alberta, Saskatchewan, etc.) | Family Day is on Monday Feb 20. |
| **Apr 7 – Apr 9** | Good Friday | Good Friday is on Friday Apr 7. |
| **May 20 – May 22** | Victoria Day | Victoria Day is on Monday May 22. |
| **Jul 1 – Jul 3** | Canada Day (observed Mon Jul 3) | Canada Day falls on Saturday; observed on Monday. |
| **Sep 2 – Sep 4** | Labour Day | Labour Day is on Monday Sep 4. |
| **Oct 7 – Oct 9** | Thanksgiving | Thanksgiving is on Monday Oct 9. |
| **Nov 11 – Nov 13** | Remembrance Day (observed Mon Nov 13) | Remembrance Day falls on Saturday; observed on Monday. |
| **Dec 23 – Dec 25** | Christmas Day | Christmas Day is on Monday Dec 25. |

> **Tip for your app:**  
> - If you need province‑specific holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario, St. Jean‑Baptiste Day in Québec, etc.), you’ll need to pull those separately.  
> - For holidays that fall on a weekend, the “observed” date is usually the following Monday, which is what creates the long weekend.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the list broken down by province or if you need additional details!
